title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: when the administration fee and the loading surcharges are charged
content:
## Charging points
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product the administration fee is charged at each approval, and the surcharges are charged at loading, when the goods are actually carried. At loading, one hazardous-cargo surcharge row is written per acceptance.

## General surcharge rule
The base surcharge per container is the category's 20-foot figure for 20-foot equipment and its 40-foot figure for 40- and 45-foot equipment. It is increased by the sum of three uplifts, added together and never compounded: the uplift of the declared class, the category's packing-group-I uplift when the packing group is I (and no packing-group uplift otherwise), and the uplift of the booking's trade lane. When the customer holds an active service contract whose tier rank is at least the category's minimum rank for the contract discount, and that minimum rank is not 0, the uplifted surcharge is then reduced by the category's contract discount percentage. The amount is the per-container figure multiplied by the container count, rounded to the cent; it is 0.00 when the acceptance's gross weight is below the category's surcharge-free weight. When the goods are marked marine pollutant, a second row is written: the category's marine pollutant rate per container multiplied by the container count.

## Conditions on booking a surcharge
- Surcharges may be booked only on an acceptance that is approved or loaded.
- Each charge code is booked once per charging date.

Both are read from the line's records: the acceptance's status, and the charges already on the acceptance's account under the same charge code.

| Acceptance status | A surcharge may be booked |
|---|---|
| approved | yes |
| loaded | yes |
| any other status | no |

## Basis Q&A
- *Is the administration fee charged at loading?* No; it is charged at each approval. The surcharges are the charges of loading.
- *How many surcharge rows can marine-pollutant goods carry at loading?* Two: the hazardous-cargo surcharge row and the second, marine pollutant row.
- *Does the weight exemption reach the marine pollutant row?* The exemption is stated for the amount of the base surcharge row; the marine pollutant row is stated as the rate multiplied by the container count.
- *May the same charge code be booked twice on one charging date?* No; each charge code is booked once per charging date.
